name: Michael Fiddelke

career.title: Joined (after starting as an intern); finance and merchandising roles, then Vice President, Pay & Benefits (2013-2015)
Senior Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis, then Merchandising Capabilities
Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer

background_rationale: Spent most of his Target career in finance roles, including financial planning and five years as CFO, before a two-year stint as COO.

notable.summary: As CEO-designate, set out three priorities for Target: strengthening merchandising authority, elevating the shopping experience and using technology to grow faster.
Days into his tenure, reshuffled senior leadership, naming a new chief merchandising officer and chief operating officer, and said Target was 'moving quickly to take action' on its priorities.
Reporting 2025 results (net sales of $104.8 billion, down 1.7%), Fiddelke called early-2026 sales momentum 'an important milestone on our path back to growth.'

Target reported second-quarter comparable sales up 3.8% and raised full-year sales guidance, with Fiddelke saying its strategy was 'resonating with our guests'; the company said it had cut prices on more than 10,000 items over the past year.

personal_story.hook: Michael Fiddelke began at Target as an intern and became its CEO about two decades later.
personal_story.summary: Fiddelke earned a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from the University of Iowa and an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management, and worked at Deloitte Consulting before joining Target. Target describes his path as a 'rise from intern to CEO'; he has been with the company since 2004. He moved through finance, merchandising, human resources and operations roles, including running pay and benefits, before becoming CFO in 2019, COO in 2024 and CEO on February 1, 2026.
